newsitem.title: USA: Sofamor bone treatment gets FDA ok for study.
newsitem.headline: Sofamor bone treatment gets FDA ok for study.

text.p: Sofamor Danek Group Inc said Monday that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has given conditional approval for Sofamor to begin a limited clinical study of its recombinant human bone morphogenetic protein.
The morphogenetic protein is a synthetically produced protein that serves as a catalyst for bone growth, company spokesman Mark Merrill said.
Conditional approval allows the product to be implanted in the lumbar spine of 12 patients to treat symptomatic degenerative disc disease, Sofamor said.
The company said approval depends upon certain modifications to its Investigational Plan within 45 days but said it sees no difficulties in complying with these conditions.
The clinical study will evaluate the potential of recombinant human bone morphogenetic protein to produce new bone to fuse the spine, Sofamor said.
The company said it will file an application for expanded clinical trials if the study is successful.
Sofamor said it is working on the bone treatment with Genetics Institute Inc, which isolated and cloned the human protein. American Home Products Corp holds a majority interest in Genetics Institute.
Sofamor Danek is focused on developing, making and marketing devices for the surgical treatment of spinal disorders.
